loading.skycraft.tip.0: Masser and Secunda each wax and wane on their own cycle. On some nights both moons are full; on others the sky is lit only by stars.
loading.skycraft.tip.1: The thirteen birthsigns can be traced faintly among the stars. The Serpent alone wanders, slipping slowly across the sky from night to night.
loading.skycraft.tip.2: Weather belongs to the land, not the world. A blizzard can howl over the Pale while the plains of Whiterun lie under a clear sky.
loading.skycraft.tip.3: The northern lights only dance over cold country on clear nights. Climb above the clouds of Skyrim after dark and look north.
loading.skycraft.tip.4: Over the ashlands of Morrowind the wind can rise into an ash storm thick enough to hide a city wall at twenty paces.
loading.skycraft.tip.5: Sneak by holding the sneak key. The eye at the centre of your view opens as those nearby grow suspicious of you.
loading.skycraft.tip.6: Sprinting and power attacks drain Stamina. Run yourself dry and you will be left walking until you catch your breath.
loading.skycraft.tip.7: Carry too much and you will be over-encumbered: no running, and every step is a slog. Sell, store or drop what you don't need.
loading.skycraft.tip.8: Each Hold keeps its own record of your crimes. A price on your head in one Hold means nothing to the guards of another.
loading.skycraft.tip.9: Guards will often accept a surrender. Yield, pay your bounty or serve your time, and the Hold forgets.
loading.skycraft.tip.10: Word Walls hold Words of Power carved in the dragon tongue. Learn a word, then spend a dragon soul to unlock it.
loading.skycraft.tip.11: A Shout must recharge before it can be used again. The more words you speak, the longer the silence that follows.
loading.skycraft.tip.12: Thirteen standing stones stand across Skyrim. Touch one to take its blessing, but you may carry only one at a time.
loading.skycraft.tip.13: Every race of Tamriel has a power it can call upon once a day. The meter beneath your Shout shows when it is ready again.
loading.skycraft.tip.14: Skills grow by use. Swing a sword to improve One-Handed; pick locks to improve Lockpicking. Enough skill increases raise your level.
loading.skycraft.tip.15: Each level brings a perk point. Spend it in the skill trees to unlock new abilities.
loading.skycraft.tip.16: Some books teach as well as tell. Reading a skill book for the first time improves the skill it describes.
loading.skycraft.tip.17: A shield in your off hand can bash a foe off balance. Time it well against a charging attacker.
loading.skycraft.tip.18: To climb, crouch and jump into a wall. Hold forward to climb, back to let yourself down, and jump backward to leap away.
loading.skycraft.tip.19: Danger grows the farther you travel from Whiterun. Wander far without preparation and the land itself will test you.
loading.skycraft.tip.20: Carriages wait outside the great cities. For a few Septims, a driver will take you to any Hold capital.
loading.skycraft.tip.21: Mark the things you use most as favourites to reach them quickly in the heat of battle.
loading.skycraft.tip.22: Trolls heal their wounds almost as fast as you can inflict them. Fire stops the healing.
loading.skycraft.tip.23: Wait or sleep to pass the hours. Some shops open only by day, and some prey only walks at night.
loading.skycraft.tip.24: In the cold your breath turns to frost. When you see it, a warm cloak and a fire are worth more than gold.
loading.skycraft.tip.25: Fireflies gather over warm meadows and forests on clear summer nights. Alchemists value what they leave behind.
loading.skycraft.tip.26: Ancient Nords were laid to rest in barrows guarded by the draugr. Many tombs are sealed with puzzles of carved stone.
loading.skycraft.tip.27: The Dwemer built cities of brass and stone deep beneath the mountains, then vanished without a trace. Their machines still stand guard.
loading.skycraft.tip.28: The Falmer were once the Snow Elves of Skyrim. Driven underground and blinded by the ages, they hunt by sound.
loading.skycraft.tip.29: Ysgramor sailed from frozen Atmora with his Five Hundred Companions. Nordic legend counts him the first of Skyrim's kings.
loading.skycraft.tip.30: The Thu'um, the Voice, is the ancient power of the dragons. Some mortals have learned it through long study; a rare few are born with it.
loading.skycraft.tip.31: High above Ivarstead, at the top of seven thousand steps, the Greybeards keep their silence. When they speak, the mountain trembles.
loading.skycraft.tip.32: The Throat of the World is the tallest mountain in Tamriel. On a clear day its peak can be seen from almost anywhere in Skyrim.
loading.skycraft.tip.33: Red Mountain dominates the island of Vvardenfell. When it wakes, ash falls across the whole of Morrowind.
loading.skycraft.tip.34: Nords believe that the bravest of the dead feast for eternity in Sovngarde, in the great Hall of Valor.
loading.skycraft.tip.35: The Daedric Princes are not gods to be worshipped lightly. Their shrines lie hidden, and their bargains always have a price.
loading.skycraft.tip.36: Black Marsh is a land of rivers, rain and mist. Outsiders who wander its swamps without a guide are rarely seen again.
loading.skycraft.tip.37: The Alik'r desert of Hammerfell can bury a caravan in sand in a single afternoon. Travel there with water and patience.
loading.skycraft.tip.38: Beyond the seas lie lands few have seen: frozen Atmora to the north, Akavir to the east, sunken Yokuda to the west.
loading.skycraft.tip.39: Dragon Priests once ruled the Nords in the name of the dragons. Their masks are said to still hold power.
loading.skycraft.tip.40: Hunters read the land. Deer graze at the forest edge at dawn, and wolves follow where the deer go.
loading.skycraft.tip.41: Smiths sell their services and their wares, but their forge, anvil and grindstone are yours to use.
loading.skycraft.tip.42: Alchemy rewards the curious. Ingredients that share an effect can be brewed together into a potion.
loading.skycraft.tip.43: Leaves drift from the trees in every forest, golden in the Rift, green in Falkreath. Stand still and watch them fall.
loading.skycraft.tip.44: A dragon's soul flows into the Dragonborn when the beast falls. Each soul can awaken a Word of Power you have learned.
loading.skycraft.tip.45: Septims bear the likeness of the Emperor. In the far corners of Tamriel, older coins still change hands.
loading.skycraft.tip.46: Mages say the stars are holes torn in the veil of Oblivion as the Aedra fled, letting the light of Aetherius shine through.
loading.skycraft.tip.47: Stuck in rock or on a ledge? The Unstuck option in the pause menu sets you back on solid ground, if you are not in combat.
command.skycraft.weather.overworld_only: Regional weather exists only in the overworld
